description: The browser job's one `e2e` line begins with an echo of a `#` — `echo "#" && scripts/nx-verdict npx nx affected --shard=3/8 -t e2e` — and takes its shard count from a literal 8 instead of the matrix. The defect this case declares is the literal; what it holds is the reading on the way there. `#` inside quotes is no comment, so the line runs `e2e`, and the target reader and this gate's own lines strip comments the same way: a reader that cut at the first `#` would see no `e2e` anywhere and fire `ci-without-e2e` before the shard rule could speak.
ciText:
# Playwright's image, mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<version>-noble, at the lockfile's version.
jobs:
  gates:
    container:
      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble # the tag before the bump: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.0-noble
      options: --user 1001
    steps:
      - run: scripts/nx-verdict npx nx affected -t lint test build check-browsers
  e2e:
    container:
      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble
      options: --user 1001
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
    steps:
      - run: echo "#" && scripts/nx-verdict npx nx affected --shard=3/8 -t e2e
